EVT-08 already says to use an interrupting event-subprocess start when the parent scope stops. The proposed guideline adds the specific case of an occurrence that stops the whole process and forbids)

refines FID-01 (The generated model collapses three separately required measured quantities (availability, quality, performance) into one generic 'Collect machine data' service task, so the reference's three service tasks have no counterpart. FID-01 already requires every distinct activity to be modeled, but it does not say how to handle several separately obtained quantities feeding one calculation. LRN-028 cove)

The reference model contradicts the description and BPMN 2.0.2 in ways a general guideline should not copy. It adds 'Repair the issue' and 'Machine worth repairing?' and 'Remaining issues?' loop steps (M2, M6, M8), which the description never states. It models the awaited occurrences 'machine restarted' and 'machine disconnected' as manual tasks (M3, M4), although these are external occurrences that should be intermediate catch events or interrupting event subprocesses. rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description says that the whole process ends when a monitored resource is disconnected or a measured figure falls below a limit, and it names no further step for the process after that point.: Give the process an explicit end event for each such ending path, placed after any action the description requires before the ending (for example, halting equipment or notifying a person as tasks). Make sure every path of the process reaches an end event, so that no sequence flow dangles and the process has at least one end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description says that the whole process ends when a monitored resource is disconnected or a measured figure falls below a limit, and it names no further step for the process after that point.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description says an external occurrence stops the whole running process at any point, with no return to the main flow.: Model that occurrence as an interrupting event subprocess inside the process, whose start event carries the occurrence's trigger type. Do not model it as a second process-level start event, and do not model it as a regular (non-event) subprocess placed in the main sequence flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description says an external occurrence stops the whole running process at any point, with no return to the main flow.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a calculation needs several distinct quantities, each of which must be obtained or retrieved separately, and then combined in that one calculation: Model each distinct quantity as its own service task that retrieves that quantity, with a label naming the quantity, placed in sequence before the calculation task. Do not merge the retrievals into one generic data-collection task, and do not omit a quantity the description requires.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a calculation needs several distinct quantities, each of which must be obtained or retrieved separately, and then combined in that one calculation

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant physically acts on a monitored resource (for example bringing it back into operation or taking it offline), and the ongoing work then continues or is halted because of that action: Model the physical action as a manual task performed by that participant, placed on the flow at the point where the description places it. Model the continued or halted work as its own task placed after that action on the sequence flow. Do not replace the action with an intermediate catch event, a start event, or a subprocess, and do not leave the continuation or halt implicit.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant physically acts on a monitored resource (for example bringing it back into operation or taking it offline), and the ongoing work then continues or is halted because of that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has a repeating cycle that collects data and checks a value, and a condition detected inside that cycle ends the process or the resource it controls, so one branch of the cycle leaves the process: Model an explicit end event at the end of each branch that leaves the cycle because of such a condition, placed after the actions that the description states for that branch. Make sure the process has at least one end event even when the description gives no other terminal outcome, so the cycle has a defined exit and no exit branch is left without an end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has a repeating cycle that collects data and checks a value, and a condition detected inside that cycle ends the process or the resource it controls, so one branch of the cycle leaves the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a condition checked repeatedly during a monitoring activity (for example a disconnection or a measured figure crossing a limit) ends the process or triggers a consequence, and the description does not say that this condition can occur at any point of the process: Model the check as an exclusive gateway placed inside the monitoring loop, after the monitoring activity. Give the branch where the condition holds the consequence tasks in the order the description gives, ending at an end event (or returning to the loop merge if the description resumes monitoring). Give the other branch a flow back to the loop's merge point. Do not model the condition as an expanded subprocess with its own start event, and do not model it as a separate start event that is not triggered by the flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a condition checked repeatedly during a monitoring activity (for example a disconnection or a measured figure crossing a limit) ends the process or triggers a consequence, and the description does not say that this condition can occur at any point of the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that when a monitored condition is met, a person must physically act on the equipment itself (for example by halting it or detaching it) before the process can continue or end: Model the physical action on the equipment as a manual task, labeled with the verb and object the description uses for it, placed in the branch that the condition's exclusive gateway opens and before the next step or the end event. Do not model that action as a start event or as an event subprocess, because the action is work a person performs and not an external occurrence the process awaits.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that when a monitored condition is met, a person must physically act on the equipment itself (for example by halting it or detaching it) before the process can continue or end
